approved_by: founder (asked for a landing page with the legal surface built out; chose scope = full legal surface incl. grievance/account-deletion/takedown pages, identity = placeholders + a supply checklist, and palette = 'keep white and Yellow only, remove dark one')
mockup_locked_by: founder (delegated — the three decisions that shape the design were made in chat: full legal surface, loud placeholders over invented values, and white+yellow with no dark surface. The rendered mockups themselves were NOT reviewed by the founder; see notes.)
notes: Two problems, one route family. (1) The landing page was the last dark surface in brand-web — /login and /dashboard were already white+yellow, so a visitor crossed a hard visual seam at signup. (2) INFLX had NO public legal surface at all: the footer's four legal links were all href="#", and grep for Omnara|grievance|CIN|GSTIN across the whole repo returned nothing. Several of the missing pages are legally mandated disclosures and one (/account-deletion) is an app-store blocker. RESEARCH DROVE THE DESIGN AND CORRECTED IT MID-BUILD. Four research agents read to primary text where reachable. Three findings changed what was built: (a) The IT Rules were amended by G.S.R. 120(E) on 10 Feb 2026, in force 20 Feb 2026 — grievance resolution dropped 15 days -> 7 DAYS, intimate-image/impersonation takedown 24h -> 2 HOURS, other removal requests 72h -> 36 HOURS, actual-knowledge takedown -> 3 HOURS. Almost every source on the Indian web still publishes the superseded figures, and a first draft written from ordinary sources would have shipped them. All mockups and the spec were rewritten. (b) The Income-tax Act 1961 was REPLACED by the Income-tax Act 2025 effective 1 Apr 2026 — the entire 194- series is repealed, so 'section 194-O' would have dated the documents instantly. Every document was drafted with NO section number and NO tax rate, phrased as 'the Income-tax Act, 2025 or any successor provision'. (c) Two research agents CONFLICTED on whether publishing ranking parameters is mandatory (notified 2020 Rules vs never-notified 2021 draft amendments). Resolved by publishing the page on its merits and never claiming it is legally required — correct under either reading. NEW RULE 3(3) (synthetically generated information, in force 20 Feb 2026) binds EVERY intermediary, not only large ones, and is carved to a follow-up in 05-impact.md — it needs upload-time declaration, a rendered label and provenance metadata, and the existing crop-to-frame uploader is exactly the kind of processing that strips metadata. Confirmed NOT applicable: all of Rule 4 (SSMI obligations attach above 50 lakh users) and any DPO requirement (that attaches only to a Significant Data Fiduciary, which is a government designation, not a threshold crossed). DPDP is notified but not enforceable until ~12 May 2027, so privacy copy is DPDP-shaped without claiming those obligations already bind. ELEVEN documents, not the ten requested — competitor research across 20+ Indian platforms plus five global creator-commerce architectures found that NOT ONE Indian creator platform publishes a shopper-facing commission disclosure, and only 3 of 9 publish a CIN; the eleventh document (How Ranking & Recommendations Work) describes INFLX's own admin-configured section/allocation engine and is the one document a competitor could not copy. Two further findings were folded in cheaply: the intermediary 'we are not the seller' line sits in the persistent footer rather than in clause 17, and a shopper-facing 'creators earn commission' notice sits on the landing page. ARCHITECTURE: legal copy is DATA (lib/legal/docs-*.js) rendered by ONE template, so a policy edit is a data edit and no document can drift structurally. Company facts live in ONE file (lib/legal/company.js) as 12 tokens; documents reference {{TOKEN}} and cannot contain a literal identity value. An unsupplied token renders as a loud red placeholder — never blank, never invented — because the worst outcome here is not a blank page but a plausible-looking fabricated CIN in a published legal document. The /legal draft banner is driven by missingTokens() so it clears itself and cannot be forgotten in place. The grievance form composes a structured complaint and hands off by email rather than POSTing to a nonexistent endpoint, and shows the response clock PER CATEGORY before submit; building it against a fake endpoint would have looked complete while silently dropping complaints. ANTI-FAKE-GREEN: the new W8 workflow was mutation-checked and THE FIRST VERSION FAILED THE CHECK — it searched rendered text for token names and passed against a build with placeholder rendering deliberately broken, because 'CIN' and 'GSTIN' also appear as ordinary footer label text. Fixed with a data-tbd attribute plus assertions that each placeholder renders visible text and names a genuinely-missing token; re-run against the same broken build it now fails correctly. Mutation reverted and diffed against a backup. VERIFIED: next build compiles, all 11 slugs prerendered; HTTP sweep of 16 routes all 200 with NO session cookie and /legal/does-not-exist 404; schema validator green across all 11 documents; greps for superseded citations and invented identity values both empty; pnpm qa GREEN 98/98 gate 0 (was 79, +19 added here). NOT VERIFIED: legal accuracy — no practitioner has reviewed these documents, which is why released stays false; founder visual review (the browser pane was contended by concurrent research agents and screenshot timed out, so verification was done against the real implementation via page-text extraction, HTTP sweep and Playwright instead of mockup renders); and whether the in-app deletion path the page instructs users to follow actually exists in the mobile app. PRODUCTION-IMPACTING, WEB ONLY — git push deploys Packages/brand-web to Vercel. No backend, no migration, no API, no OTA, no APK. Explicit founder go required before push. GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md lists the 12 facts the founder must supply and the six promises the product must now make true.

release.phased: SHIPPED IN TWO PHASES on the founder's call, after they loaded inflx.in and found it still dark — everything built here was local and unpushed at that point. PHASE 1 (this commit): the landing page only — app/page.js restyled to white+yellow, app/layout.js public metadata, SiteFooter, RichText, lib/legal/company.js and lib/legal/nav.js. PHASE 2 (held): all eleven legal documents, /legal/**, /contact, /account-deletion, SiteHeader, DocPage, GrievanceForm, docs-*.js, registry.js and qa/web/brand/legal-surface.spec.ts stay UNCOMMITTED until the founder supplies the statutory facts. Reason: deploying the legal pages today would publish legal documents with visible red placeholders where a CIN and a named Grievance Officer belong, which is a worse public artefact than the dark landing page it replaces. The seam is held by LEGAL_SURFACE_LIVE in lib/legal/nav.js — while false the footer shows the company identity and the ownership notice only, with no link to an unpublished page and no half-filled statutory block. Flipping it to true, supplying company.js and committing app/legal/** are ONE change; they do not make sense apart. The phase-1 commit's dependency graph was checked to be closed (page.js -> SiteFooter -> company/nav/RichText/Logo) so the partial commit cannot break the Vercel build. qa/web/brand/landing-footer.spec.ts ships with phase 1 and is phase-AWARE rather than skipped — it asserts no dead links, no public placeholder, the ownership notice, and zero dark surfaces measured from rendered backgrounds; the legal-route workflows ship with phase 2. No test was skipped to achieve this.
release.qa_run: pnpm qa GREEN — 98/98 workflows passed (40.1s), 2026-08-04, gate 0. Baseline before this contract was 79/79; the 19 added here are the public legal surface workflow.

(1) The 12 mandatory disclosures in Packages/brand-web/lib/legal/company.js are still null — CIN, GSTIN, registered address, Grievance Officer name/designation/email, customer-care email/mobile/landline, effective date, jurisdiction city. Publishing legal documents with these unfilled is not an option, and the pages say so themselves. (2) No licensed practitioner has reviewed the documents. See GO-LIVE-CHECKLIST.md.
